subject: MSA + SOW indemnity: proposed narrow third-party carve for Infratech
content:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@infratech.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: rajiv.patel@infratech.com, procurement@infratech.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form - indemnity redlines

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending the MSA and SOW. We reviewed with our legal team and have a narrow ask on the third-party infringement indemnity: we need a carve that limits Redwood's obligation to claims based on (i) Redwood modifications to the model or (ii) customer-provided prompt/data that directly causes infringement. In short, Infratech wants to avoid taking risk for pre-trained model IP or for output where we provided the proprietary content that created the output.

Attached is a marked PDF (Infratech_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) that shows the suggested language. Two quick notes:
- We are not asking for a wholesale removal of the indemnity - just an explicit allocation where customer-controlled inputs are the trigger.
- We will accept cooperation/defense control where Redwood defends but only seeks reasonable involvement from Infratech (e.g., we won't provide engineers for long depositions).

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept something along these lines? If not, what narrow alternative would you propose? Also copying procurement and Rajiv to ensure we don't miss SOW impacts.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Cole
Head of Legal Operations
Infratech Inc.

---
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@infratech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form - indemnity redlines

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear markup and the narrow ask. I pulled Karthik and Irene into thread for legal/ops take. Quick operational reply from us: we can consider narrowing the trigger as you requested, but there are three constraints that matter to Redwood and to our broader customer base:

1) Pre-trained model IP: we can narrow the indemnity to exclude claims that arise solely from pre-training on third-party corpora, provided the customer accepts an explicit ship of risk for outputs that reproduce identified third-party content.

2) Customer-provided prompt/data: we are open to a prompt/source-based carve but need objective criteria (e.g., timestamped customer content, file hashes) and a discovery commitment so we can validate the causal link.

3) Defense control / cooperation: we generally retain defense control for efficiency, but we can commit to reasonable consultation and to not requiring customer attendance at routine technical interviews. If Infratech wants to take control of defense for a limited class of claims, we can discuss an escrow/indemnity fee or insurance offset.

Karthik — can you review Samantha's redline and propose suggested language that maps to these constraints? Marcus / Irene — any commercial/ops impacts on the SOW pricing if we accept a narrower trigger (e.g., higher SOW margin to offset residual risk)?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@infratech.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form - indemnity redlines

Priya / Samantha —

Thanks — I took Samantha's PDF and drafted two short alternatives in the attached doc (OrderForm_SOW_Infratech_20270320.docx). High-level comparison:

Option A (customer-input carve):
- Redwood indemnifies for third-party IP claims except where the claim arises solely from customer-provided prompts or data that are proven, by clear and convincing evidence, to be the proximate cause of the infringing output.
- Customer must provide preserved originals (files, prompt logs) within 7 days of notice and cooperate in technical review.

Option B (shared risk with insurance ladder):
- Redwood accepts indemnity for model-derived claims but customer agrees to an insurance-first procedure: customer submits claim to its insurance first; if insurer denies, Redwood will step in subject to a cap equal to the order form value.

My recommendation: start with Option A as it aligns with your ask and is operationally tractable. We need to define "proximate cause" narrowly to avoid broad discovery. Proposed language below (simplified for thread):

"Redwood will indemnify Customer from third-party claims alleging that the output delivered by the Services infringes a third party's intellectual property, except where (a) the claim arises solely from Customer-provided input or data, and (b) Customer fails to produce the preserved input or otherwise refuses to cooperate in the defense. In such case Redwood's obligation shall be limited to the extent caused by Redwood's modifications to the model or serving layer."

Samantha — if that maps to your markup, we can circulate a redline for final signoff. If Infratech insists on defense control, we should discuss a modest SOW uplift or a carve-limited term.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

---
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@infratech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@infratech.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form - indemnity redlines

Karthik / Priya —

Option A looks reasonable. A couple clarifications before we circulate a redline back to procurement:
- The 7-day preservation window is tight for our legal ops team; can we make that 14 days?
- We prefer language that allows us to request 'reasonable' defense participation rather than blanket refusal for depositions — e.g., "Customer will not be required to produce engineering staff for routine depositions but will make technical SMEs reasonably available for written discovery and one-day interviews."

If Redwood can accept 14-day preservation and the SME language above, we'll convert Karthik's suggested clause into our final redline and get procurement to sign off. We also won't push for defense control if the scope carve exists.

Thanks,
Samantha

---
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@infratech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & Order Form - indemnity redlines

Thanks Samantha — we can accept the 14-day preservation window and the "reasonable SME availability" language. Marcus, per our pricing playbook, please calculate a nominal uplift (we typically add 1-1.5% of Order Form value for indemnity carve concessions) and put that in the SOW appendix. Irene — update the evidence checklist and add the file-hash/timestamp examples for preserved inputs.

I'll circulate a final redline (clean + marked) by EOD tomorrow for Infratech procurement and legal to review. Once we have their signoff we'll route for DocuSign (link attached).

Cheers,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Infratech_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf), OrderForm_SOW_Infratech_20270320.docx (docx)
